en.velora.home.answer.0: Yes — every component and the full landing template are MIT licensed. Use them in personal and commercial projects, no attribution required.
en.velora.home.faq.1: How is this different from Magic UI?  +
en.velora.home.answer.1: Velora ships complete, assembled landing pages — not just isolated components. Every animation respects prefers-reduced-motion, causes zero layout shift, and is tuned for mobile.
en.velora.home.answer.2: The original uses Next.js 16, React 19, Tailwind CSS 4, shadcn/ui and Motion. This Unity adaptation uses converted UXML/USS and Neo.HtmlToUitk runtime components.
en.velora.home.answer.3: Yes. The SaaS template is free forever. Additional niches and section variants land in Velora Pro.

en.velora.about.title: Landing-page polish
en.velora.about.description: Velora UI started with a simple observation: the animated-component market charges premium prices for what is, at its core, CSS variables and a motion library. We think that layer should be free.
en.velora.about.story.one: The React ecosystem settled on a great pattern: copy the component into your project, own the code. But the libraries that popularized animated marketing components put their best work — the assembled, multi-page templates — behind $149–$299 paywalls, hardcode their brand colors into every snippet, and rarely tell you what an effect costs in kilobytes.
en.velora.about.story.two: Velora is the version of that idea we wanted to exist: every component wired to your design tokens, every animation accountable for its bundle size and its motion-sensitivity behavior, and the complete template — blog, pricing, auth, changelog and all — free under MIT.
en.velora.about.principles.title: What we optimize for
en.velora.principle.body.0: The complete template — not a teaser — is MIT licensed. Pro adds breadth for teams, but nothing on this site is held back.
en.velora.principle.body.1: Every component publishes its gzipped size and dependency count. No three.js payloads hiding behind a pretty demo.
en.velora.principle.body.2: prefers-reduced-motion is respected globally, keyboard focus stays visible, and markup stays semantic.
en.velora.principle.body.3: Components read shadcn CSS variables. Rebrand the entire system — every gradient, beam and glow — by changing one token block.
en.velora.adaptation.title: This is a Unity adaptation
en.velora.adaptation.body: The source content and layout come from Velora UI (MIT). HTML/CSS was adapted to the supported converter subset, then converted by the real HtmlToUitk CLI. Native UITK handles navigation, media queries and keyframes. Small typed C# bindings replace the original React interactions. Open the original to compare.
